new_destinations.name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park' (a guidebook chapter) and the Discover Tasmania North West page; CROSS-REGION names it 'Cradle Mountain'. Flagship Tasmanian park (World Heritage), so rank 1-2 exemption applies besides its nine spots.

new_destinations.name: Devonport
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Devonport' page (with its own See list) and the 'Western Tasmania' region page; Discover Tasmania North West page. Regional city and Spirit of Tasmania ferry port.

new_destinations.name: Burnie
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Burnie' page lists the penguin centre, garden and Guide Falls; regional city.

new_destinations.name: Wynyard
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Wynyard' page (Table Cape, Fossil Bluff, the Rocky Cape coast) and 'Western Tasmania' page; Table Cape tulips are the area's headline.

new_destinations.name: Stanley
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Stanley (Tasmania)' page and 'Western Tasmania'; The Nut is a named headline attraction. The town is the destination, so it is not also a spot.

new_destinations.name: Mole Creek Karst National Park
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Mole Creek' page (the caves and Devils Gullet) and Parks Tasmania; the park is named for the caves. Deloraine and Big Coffee Pot are its gateway spots (Wikivoyage Deloraine page).

kept_total_note: 45 placed spots plus 4 kept candidates that became the destinations themselves (Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair NP, Devonport, Stanley, Mole Creek Karst NP); Beaconsfield Mine is kept but owned by tas-launceston-northeast.

lowest_kept.name: Marion's Lookout
lowest_kept.reason: Named Wikivoyage day walk (2 h return) to a Dove Lake viewpoint; a distinct half-day outing (rules 1-2).

lowest_kept.name: Pencil Pine Falls
lowest_kept.reason: Short boardwalk rainforest walk behind the visitor centre; Wikivoyage calls it a must for all visitors.

lowest_kept.name: Waldheim Chalet
lowest_kept.reason: Gustav Weindorfer's 1912 chalet with displays; a heritage site visitors can enter, named by the guide (rules 1-2).

lowest_kept.name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk
lowest_kept.reason: The headline day walk to the summit of Cradle Mountain from Dove Lake; Wikivoyage names it (rule 1).

lowest_kept.name: Devils Gullet
lowest_kept.reason: Named lookout platform over a sheer cliff with views to Cradle Mountain, near Mole Creek (rules 1-2).

lowest_kept.name: King Solomon's Cave
lowest_kept.reason: Show cave in the Mole Creek Karst, listed by Wikivoyage (rules 1-2).

lowest_kept.name: Marakoopa Cave
lowest_kept.reason: Glow-worm show cave in Mole Creek Karst, listed by Wikivoyage; a distinct tour.

lowest_kept.name: Walls of Jerusalem Multi-Day Walk
lowest_kept.reason: Promoted multi-day loop in the national park (benchmark: Hump Ridge Track).

stronger_left_out.name: Pool of Bethesda
stronger_left_out.reason: Views and coordinates belong to the biblical pool in Jerusalem; the Tasmanian tarn has one counted source and is a side feature of a multi-day walk (rule 3). Script reject, audit review: held for the owner.

stronger_left_out.name: Ulverstone
stronger_left_out.reason: Wikivoyage page lists only cafes, a volunteer-run history museum and surrounding sites (Lillico Beach, Leven Canyon); the town has no own draw.

stronger_left_out.name: Penguin
stronger_left_out.reason: Seaside town with the Big Penguin icon, heritage trail and beach; Wikivoyage lists it only as 'home of the Big Penguin', no town page.

stronger_left_out.name: Takayna / Tarkine
stronger_left_out.reason: Named by Discover Tasmania as a wilderness region of rainforest and coast; a region, not one place.

stronger_left_out.name: Smithton
stronger_left_out.reason: Dairy town and base for the Circular Head area per Wikivoyage.

stronger_left_out.name: Beaconsfield
stronger_left_out.reason: Town wrapper beside its own attraction, Beaconsfield Mine and Heritage Centre (WIKI: town only a spot when the town is itself a draw).

stronger_left_out.name: Latrobe
stronger_left_out.reason: Historic town with Gilbert Street heritage, Axemans Hall of Fame and platypus viewing; only one real-sourced listing (Wikivoyage Latrobe (Tasmania) page); town itself is a modest draw.

stronger_left_out.name: Mole Creek
stronger_left_out.reason: Town beside Mole Creek Karst, the caves' base; two Wikivoyage pages.

stronger_left_out.name: Somerset Beach
stronger_left_out.reason: Wikivoyage Burnie and Western Tasmania: swimming beach along Somerset coast, but the pin is the Somerset town centre point.

stronger_left_out.name: Somerset
stronger_left_out.reason: Small coastal town with a beach; no sight of its own named by the guide.

stronger_left_out.name: Arthur River
stronger_left_out.reason: Gateway village for the Tarkine / Edge of the World drive; draws are beyond it (benchmark: Pipiriki).

stronger_left_out.name: Great Western Tiers
stronger_left_out.reason: A broad escarpment/range of many walks, not one place (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Greens Beach
stronger_left_out.reason: Ambiguous: the source may mean the Marrawah surf beach or Greens Beach at the Tamar mouth (candidate coordinates -41.085,146.740 are the latter); not placed until resolved (CROSS-REGION).

stronger_left_out.name: Barn Bluff
stronger_left_out.reason: Named Wikivoyage mountain climb off the Overland Track; real but 10 h and for experienced walkers.

stronger_left_out.name: Hellyer Gorge
stronger_left_out.reason: Walking tracks along the Hellyer River, named by Wikivoyage.

stronger_left_out.name: King David's Peak
stronger_left_out.reason: A peak climbed within the Walls of Jerusalem trip (rule 3).

stronger_left_out.name: Cathedral Mountain
stronger_left_out.reason: Peak seen from the Overland Track; no specific visitor outing in the source (rule 2).

stronger_left_out.name: Dial Range
stronger_left_out.reason: Coastal walks with views over Penguin, Wikivoyage 'Do' entry.

stronger_left_out.name: Enchanted Walk
stronger_left_out.reason: Half-hour dry walk past waterfalls and rainforest, named by Wikivoyage.

review_for_owner: Penguin General Cemetery and Vantage Point
benchmark: NZ-specific benchmarks do not apply to Tasmania. Negative benchmarks held: events (Sheffield Mural Fest) excluded, a cemetery lookout (Penguin General Cemetery) held for review, town wrappers (Beaconsfield, Latrobe, Mole Creek, Ulverstone, Penguin, Smithton) not placed beside their attractions, a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond (Arthur River) is review, not kept.
